kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Pre-Islamic Arabization of Biblical Hebrew שְׁמוּאֵל (šəmūʾēl). Chiefly borne by Jews. The forms سَمَوْئِيل (samawʔīl), سَمَوِيل (samawīl) are typically Christian, although also encountered for ethnic Jews. Later borrowed again as شَمَوْئِيل (šamawʔīl), شَمَوِيل (šamawīl), apparently supported by the Classical Syriac form ܫܡܘܝܠ, but now most popular for referring to Israeli Hebrew men. Lastly, forms like صَمُوئِل (ṣamūʔil), صَمُوئِيل (ṣamūʔīl), صَمْوِيل (ṣamwīl) are from European languages including English.
g: a male given name, equivalent to English Samuel
